verdict.rationale: Honcho documents several of its own pieces that point toward shared-versus-private memory. It can model state about groups as well as users and agents. Its multi-peer perspective tracks what one peer knows about another, which implies per-peer visibility. Retrieval supports peer scoping, and named-scope API keys can be bound to a single scope that has member sessions. However, none of the evidence explicitly describes choosing which memory to share across a team or group while keeping other memory private. missing for 10: explicit documentation of shared/team memory with selective sharing, a documented privacy or visibility model for per-peer private memory, access-control details beyond scoped keys, independent or hands-on corroboration.
